messages:
sam: Hey folks — customer on Dedicated (VPC) moved their L7 from ELB -> Istio sidecar + internal LB yesterday and now getting intermittent 403s for API calls that include an opaque SSO token. They say it used to work. Repro below, can someone triage?

riyad: Thanks, can you paste a curl repro and the backend request headers (what our service sees)?

sam: Repro steps:
1) From client inside customer VPC:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <OPAQUE_TOKEN>" https://api.customer.example/v1/generate -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n"
```
2) Response: 403  (service returns 403 when mounted behind our L7 -> istio path)

3) On our backend (service logs) header snapshot:
```
Received headers:
host: api.customer.example
x-forwarded-for: 10.12.4.5
x-forwarded-proto: https
user-agent: curl/7.68.0
content-length: 0
# NO Authorization header at all
```

sam: We suspect the Istio LB or Envoy filter is dropping or rewriting Authorization -> cookie or x-opaque-token. Customer says they have a custom auth proxy before our gateway as well.

caroline: Any LB type? NLB vs ALB? NLB preserves TCP, ALB can strip. Also did they enable proxy protocol?

sam: They are on an internal ALB in front of Istio ingress (AWS). Proxy-proto off. No WAF.

riyad: Have you checked Istio TrafficPolicy or AuthorizationPolicy that may be removing headers? Also Istio's envoys have header normalization and :method pseudo header ordering quirks. Can you capture Envoy access logs at the Istio ingress?

sam: Pasted an ingress pod Envoy admin /proxy-log snippet:
```
[2026-03-10T14:23:11.123Z] "GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1" 403 - via envoy, request_headers:
":method: GET"
":path: /v1/generate"
"host: api.customer.example"
"x-forwarded-for: 10.12.4.5"
# again no Authorization header present
```

mike: This looks like header removal earlier in the chain. Two hypotheses: (1) ALB is forwarding Authorization as part of HTTP but an intermediate ingress route or Istio filter rewrites/removes it; (2) customer proxy terminates TLS and reissues requests without Authorization. Ask customer for tcpdump (or s2i capture) on the ALB target instance to confirm header at that point.

sam: Customer captured at their proxy and shows Authorization preserved to ALB. They claim the ALB -> Istio ingress path is where it vanishes.

caroline: Could be an IstioRequestAuthentication / AuthorizationPolicy using 'origins' JWT that rejects unknown opaque tokens and intentionally removes header for security. Check for a policy like:
```
apiVersion: "security.istio.io/v1beta1"
kind: RequestAuthentication
metadata:
  name: jwt-auth
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: gateway
  jwtRules:
  - issuer: "https://sso.corp.example"
    jwksUri: "https://sso.corp.example/.well-known/jwks.json"
```
If a policy fails, Istio could block/return 401/403. But that wouldn't silently drop header; it would reject earlier.

riyad: Another angle: our gateway (Redwood Dedicated L7) has an optional header-sanitizer feature that strips 'Authorization' and emits 'x-authorization-opaque' for opaque tokens processed by our authz filter. If misconfigured during a rollout, it could strip and not forward the transformed header. Check config map 'dedicated-proxy.header-sanitizer.enabled' and the envoy filter chain.

sam: Found config in the customer's dedicated config: "sanitize_auth: true" under our gateway profile. They didn't know it was enabled.

support-bot: Automated check: dedicated-proxy header-sanitizer feature flagged in customer config (sanitize_auth=true). Known issue: if downstream expects Authorization to be rewritten back, older runtime 0.9.3 can drop it. Suggested action: toggle sanitize_auth=false OR upgrade runtime to >=0.9.5 where rewritten header x-authorization-opaque is set.

sam: Ok we'll ask customer to toggle sanitize_auth=false for quick repro.

caroline: While toggling, also check if Istio has any envoyFilter that rewrites or sets remove_headers. Example problematic filter config: 
```
- applyTo: HTTP_FILTER
  match:
    context: GATEWAY
  patch:
    operation: MERGE
    value:
      typed_config:
        '@type': type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.header_to_metadata.v3.Config
        request_rules:
        - header: Authorization
          on_header_present:
            metadata_namespace: envoy.filters.http.header_to_metadata
            key: auth_present
```
This can unexpectedly mutate header flows.
```

riyad: If toggle fixes it, plan: roll forward runtime patch 0.9.5 and notify customer to re-enable sanitize_auth with the runtime fix. Also add an audit check to the console to warn about sanitize_auth=true on older runtimes.

sam: Customer toggled sanitize_auth=false and now requests are validated and Authorization reaches backend; 200 responses observed. They want root cause.

mike: Root cause summary for the ticket: dedicated gateway header-sanitizer feature enabled on older runtime (0.9.3) had a bug that dropped Authorization when combined with Istio-based ingress filter ordering. The combination caused our auth mask to remove header but not set the fallback header. Workaround: set sanitize_auth=false. Fix: upgrade runtime to 0.9.5 where header forwarding is fixed and add console warning.

caroline: I'll file a release note and a console validation rule. Can someone add repro steps and a test case to the infra-e2e suite to catch this?

riyad: I'll take e2e test. sam — can you attach the minimal manifest + config we used to reproduce?

sam: Attaching gist of the customer's minimal config and the curl we used. Also adding the envoy access log diff. Will raise the support ticket update. :thumbsup:

support-bot: Ticket updated: workaround applied, recommended runtime upgrade, assigned to eng-infra for patch (inc-4521).
